title: Analyzing US Census Data
text:
This chart compares state populations in 2019 and 2023 and calculates the percent change over that period.









Key Takeaways:

Mountain West & South boom: Idaho (+9.9%), Utah (+6.6%), Montana (+6.0%), Delaware (+6.0%), and Florida (+5.3%) grew the fastest between 2019 and 2023.
Population declines: Washington, D.C. (-3.8%), Louisiana (-1.6%), and California (-1.4%) saw the largest percentage drops over the same period.

title: Analyzing US Census Data
text:
Median household income by state
This chart shows median household income across states in 2023.









Key Takeaways:

Top earners: Washington, D.C. ($108,210), Massachusetts ($99,858), New Jersey ($99,781), and Maryland ($98,678) lead in median household income.
Wide gap: There is nearly a $55,000 gap between the highest-income state (Massachusetts) and the lowest-income state (Mississippi at $54,203).

title: Analyzing US Census Data
section: Population growth and median household income
text:
Population growth and median household income
This chart compares each state’s population change (2019–2023) with its 2023 median household income to explore how population growth relates to economic prosperity.









Key Takeaways:

Positive but modest relationship: The upward-sloping dashed trend line shows that states with higher median household incomes tend to have slightly higher population growth overall.
Cost of living matters: Some of the fastest-growing states (like Idaho, Montana, and Florida) have middle-tier incomes, suggesting that lower housing costs and remote-work migration played a major role alongside wages.

title: Analyzing US Census Data
text:
Fastest-growing U.S. counties
This chart downloads county-level population estimates from the 2019 and 2023 5-year ACS and highlights the 15 fastest-growing counties (among counties with at least 10,000 residents).









County Growth Facts:

#1 Fastest-Growing County: Madison County, Idaho surged by 37.0% (growing from 39,100 to 53,578 residents).
Texas Suburban Boom: Five of the top 10 fastest-growing counties in the nation are in Texas—led by Kaufman County (+29.8%), Comal County (+23.2%), Bastrop County (+21.1%), Rockwall County (+20.3%), and Hays County (+20.2%).
Most New Residents Overall: Maricopa County, Arizona (Phoenix area) added the most people in total (+163,177 residents), followed by Collin County, Texas (+142,624) and Harris County, Texas (+111,949).

title: About This Project
text:
This project examines population growth and economic development using data from the U.S. Census Bureau.
Most of the charts use data from the American Community Survey, which estimates population, income, education, and other characteristics across the United States.
Data source: U.S. Census Bureau

title: Population Growth and Economic Development
text:
U.S. Economic Landscape Across States


This website uses data from the U.S. Census Bureau to explore population growth and economic development across the United States.



Which states have grown fastest?
How do states differ in median household income?
How might population change be related to economic opportunity?





Fastest-Growing State: Idaho led the nation with nearly 10% population growth (followed by Utah at 6.6% and Montana at 6.0%).
Fastest-Growing Counties: Madison County, Idaho (+37.0%) and Kaufman County, Texas (+29.8%) topped all U.S. counties in percentage growth, while Maricopa County, Arizona added the most new residents (+163,177).
Highest Median Income: Washington, D.C. ($108,210), Massachusetts ($99,858), and New Jersey ($99,781) had the highest median household incomes in 2023.
Surprising Trend: Higher income doesn’t always mean faster growth—many fast-growing states in the Mountain West and South have moderate median incomes but lower costs of living.

Visit the Analysis page to see charts based on American Community Survey data.
